To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
V2V and multi-hop V2R communications can effectively support vehicular sensor networks, and can be easily deployed through the adoption of off-the-shelf hardware.

1) the use of short range communications in vehicular networks can be an effective alternative to the cellular network, especially for data transmission; 2) the adoption of multi-hop communications is essential for the success of V2V and/or V2R networks; 3) the use of multi-hop communications can be effectively implemented through a simple but effective algorithm; 4) the adoption of a field trial, even if small, can provide valuable information about the performance of the proposed algorithm.

(a) multi-hop V2V/V2R communications allow to increase the amount of data transmitted without using cellular network resources; (b) the proposed routing algorithm is simple and effective; (c) the field trial shows the feasibility of multi-hop V2X communications in urban scenarios.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and evaluation, in a realistic urban setting, of a multi-hop routing algorithm to be used in a vehicular sensor network, with the aim of reducing the load on cellular network.
a new paradigm of vehicular sensor network (VSN) communications, where the vehicles are used as sensors to collect data and as routers to forward data.
the design, simulation and validation of a novel multi-hop communication protocol for vehicular networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed multi-hop algorithm is a valid solution to reduce the cellular traffic in urban scenarios.
our proposed routing algorithm, in conjunction with the IEEE802.11p protocol, is a viable alternative to cellular communication for data delivery in vehicular networks.
our proposal is a viable solution for data delivery in vehicular sensor networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed multi-hop algorithm can be easily implemented in vehicular networks and it can be used to improve the efficiency of data collection.
the proposed algorithm can be used as a first step towards an efficient multi-hop communication system for vehicular sensor network.
we propose and validate through simulation and real testbed an algorithm for multi-hop data forwarding in vehicular sensor networks, with the aim to reduce the load on cellular networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed routing scheme is simple to implement, and can be used to reduce cellular traffic by 30%, with the consequent benefits in terms of energy savings and bandwidth usage.
V2V and multi-hop V2R communications are a valid alternative to cellular networks, and can be used to offload the cellular network and increase the amount of data collected on board.
the proposed algorithm, with its simple implementation and low cost, can be easily adopted by the automotive industry to implement multi-hop communications in vehicular sensor networks.
